what_proposed: No changes are planned for Woodlawn at this time. Woodlawn would remain open as a neighborhood K-5 school with its current grades and school boundary.
what_gain: Keeping the neighborhood school: Students keep their familiar teachers, staff, and walk-to-school community.
what_else_considered: Surrounding space limits: Woodlawn would continue serving its neighborhood community because surrounding schools were not an option for boosting enrollment or consolidation because of limited space for students.

why_considering: Low enrollment numbers: Both Woodmere and Whitman face enrollment challenges below district enrollment goals, with Woodmere remaining in the low 220s. Central school space: Whitman is closer to where students live, has additional space improvements.
what_proposed: Woodmere School would close as a school building. 100% of its neighborhood K-5 school boundary would shift to Whitman K-5. Middle and high school pathway: All students in this combined boundary move to Brentwood Middle School and then to Franklin High School.
what_gain: Full student support: Combining school communities gives students access to more classmates, full-time staff, and stable classroom support.
what_else_considered: Whitman was selected as the receiving school over Woodmere because of its central location relative to where students live.
what_about_special_ed: The Communication Behavior (CB) classrooms currently located at Woodmere would be moved to Kelly Elementary. The Special Education Department would work together with the school team and families to identify individual student placements for the upcoming school year: Special education classrooms: Provided in the CB Classrooms at Kelly Elementary. Move to Whitman Elementary: Joining a neighborhood school supporting students with and without disabilities. As a neighborhood school supporting students with and without disabilities, Whitman provides the full range of special education services. School teams would contact families in the coming weeks to discuss individual move plans and answer any questions.

why_considering: Strengthening DLI learning Moving the Mandarin DLI program from Clark to Woodstock strengthens the DLI learning at a single school. Clark DLI enrollment is too small: Clark's current Mandarin DLI kindergarten class is fewer than 8 students, making a separate program too small.
what_proposed: Woodstock would remain open as a neighborhood K-5 school and receive the Mandarin Dual Language Immersion (DLI) program from Clark K-5.
what_gain: Vibrant language community: Bringing together the program at Woodstock builds one language program with enough students to continue and creates a school-wide culture centered on language learning. Teacher teamwork: Enables DLI teachers to work together, plan together, and grow alongside fellow language educators.
what_else_considered: Keeping the program going: Concentrating Mandarin DLI programs at Woodstock expands program support and supports teacher collaboration.
what_about_special_ed: The Communication Behavior Classrooms currently located at Lewis Elementary School will be relocated to Woodstock Elementary School and join the current K-5 CB classroom. To ensure a seamless transition, school and district leaders will conduct site walk-throughs to evaluate programmatic readiness, space, transportation, and ADA accessibility. Special education administrators will work closely with school principals to ensure every site is prepared to meet student IEP requirements.
